an3.91:1.3: Resident monastics do not merely stay at a monastery, they undertake the responsibility of looking after the place and its community. The commentary here is of interest, as it is a rare use of the term _bhārāhara_ outside the context of the Bhārasutta ([sn22.12]()). It says, “Resident means the one who bears the burden of setting up new monasteries and taking care of old ones.” This agrees with the description of Kassapagotta at [pli-tv-kd9:1.1.3](): “He was dedicated to the local monastery, trying to get good monks to come, to help those who had come be comfortable, and to make the local monastery grow and reach maturity.” See [an6.54:1.2]() for a monk who abused this responsibility.
